ADM_LEVELS.ui.transportHint: A token inside this region does not sink in water and is not affected by region auras. Attach the region to a tile (Mass Edit) so it moves with the cart. Set the region's elevation range so a flying token above is not counted inside.
ADM_LEVELS.ui.waterHint: A token with elevation ≤ surface gets the «Swimming» status and Swim movement.
ADM_LEVELS.ui.disableHint: ADMaps Tools logic is ignored for this region. Settings are kept.
ADM_LEVELS.ui.tileBindHint: The region is active/disabled in sync with the tile's visibility.
ADM_LEVELS.ui.clickTile: Click a tile on the map (Esc — cancel).
ADM_LEVELS.wall.hint:
Normal wall: follows the tile's visibility (tile visible → wall active, tile hidden → passable). The original move/sight is saved on binding.
Door / Secret door: controls the tile's visibility (open → tile visible, closed → hidden).
ADM_LEVELS.videoSkip.label: Pause between shows
ADM_LEVELS.videoSkip.hint: For a video tile: after each playback, hide it for N (or random N–M) clip durations, then show again. Empty — normal infinite loop. Example: «1-2» — birds fly across, pause 1–2 flybys, then again.
ADM_LEVELS.videoSkip.poolHint: On — on EACH show a random video clip from the SAME FOLDER as the tile image above. Resolved by the GM and broadcast to everyone (players lack file-browse permission). Off — the single set clip.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.roofFogFix.name: Roof fog fix
ADM_LEVELS.settings.roofFogFix.hint: After a token stops, forces a vision/occlusion refresh — clears the stale black fog-of-war left when a token exits from under a Better Roofs roof tile. Only acts when Better Roofs is active and roofs are present.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tokenSort.name: Auto token z-order
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tokenSort.hint: Smaller tokens render on top of larger ones (by footprint); the active combatant / last-moved token is raised within its size tier. Writes the token sort field (GM only).
ADM_LEVELS.wallHeightFilter.floorTip: Shows the walls of the selected floor. A wall that ends exactly at «bottom», or starts exactly at «top», belongs to the neighbouring floor and is hidden. If «top» is not greater than «bottom», the upper bound counts as unset.
ADM_LEVELS.wallHeightFilter.unsetTip: Walls with no height set at all count as full-height (from −∞ to +∞) and cross every floor. Uncheck to hide them as well.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.wallHeightFilter.hin: A toggle in the walls layer toolbar: show only the walls of the selected floor, so that lower-floor walls do not get in the way when editing upper ones. Hidden walls can neither be seen nor selected — not by clicking, not by a selection box. The band is set by the «bottom» and «top» fields; a wall that ends exactly at «bottom» belongs to the floor below and is hidden. Walls with no height set count as full-height and have their own checkbox. Applies only on the walls layer and changes nothing in the scene itself.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.teleportFix.name: Teleports on transfer
ADM_LEVELS.settings.teleportFix.hint: Rewrites «Teleport Token» region-behavior destinations whenever regions move to another scene — otherwise the teleport keeps pointing at the source scene. Three cases: (1) scene duplicated — automatic on scene creation; (2) scene moved to another world as a JSON file — automatic on import, using the export marker written by the «Scene export name» tool (which is also needed on the importing side); (3) regions pasted into an existing scene (Mass Edit preset, copy&paste, drag&drop) — automatic right after the paste. In cases 2 and 3 only teleports whose destination travelled along are touched: deliberate cross-scene teleports are left alone. Scenes that arrived before the tool was enabled can be repaired from the scene context menu.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tokenReanimator.name: Video reanimator (WEBM)
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tokenReanimator.hint: Keeps the PIXI ticker alive and resumes frozen WEBM/video on the canvas (tiles, tokens, weather, effects) — these often stop when rings/overlays are added to tokens or by other modules. Periodic guard + reaction to scene/token events.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tokenDrop.name: Token drop from folder
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tokenDrop.hint: Drag an actor folder onto the scene to enter placement mode: tokens are laid out wall-aware (breadth-first, nobody behind a wall), the preview follows the cursor, the wheel cycles layouts, a click places them, Esc cancels. Alt while dropping creates them hidden. Dragging is native, so folders can still be rearranged within the sidebar. GM only.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tileControl.name: Tile control panel
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tileControl.hint: A button in the tiles tools opens a side panel: list of layer tiles by Z-order, click = control the tile + isolation (an overlapped tile can be moved/rotated directly on the canvas), hover = highlight, double-click = zoom, search, Alt+↑/↓ = z-order. Right-click a row (with Mass Edit) — disable attached walls/regions.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.propsAutoPos.name: Tile auto-align
ADM_LEVELS.settings.propsAutoPos.hint: A crosshair button in the Tile HUD (right-click a tile): puts the tile or prop back where it sat on the original map. The spot is found by matching the tile's pixels against the scene background — a coarse pass first, then a fine one — so the tile needs actual detail: a flat or nearly transparent image has nothing to match on. A scaled tile matches poorly, because its pixel size no longer lines up with the background; the tool warns about that. GM only.

ADMaps_PropsAutoPos.Placed: Tile placed at ({x}, {y}). Avg err: {err} | {count} points | {time}ms
ADMaps_PropsAutoPos.TooFlat: Not enough detail pixels in tile ({count}). Tile is too flat — matching not possible.
ADMaps_PropsAutoPos.ScaledWarn: Tile is scaled! Pixel size doesn't match canvas size — accuracy may suffer.

ADM_LEVELS.settings.sceneFlip.name: Scene flip / rotate
ADM_LEVELS.settings.sceneFlip.hint: Right-click a scene in the navbar → «Scene Flip» → mirror horizontally/vertically or rotate 180° (background, tiles, walls, regions, lights, sounds, notes, drawings; tokens untouched) + reset to original. GM only.

Notify.GMOnly: Only the GM can flip scenes.
Notify.InProgress: A flip is already running for this scene.
Notify.NothingToReset: Nothing to reset for this scene.

ADM_LEVELS.settings.sceneSwitch.name: Scene variations
ADM_LEVELS.settings.sceneSwitch.hint: Right-click a scene in the navbar → «Variations»: switch between prepared takes on the same map — different backgrounds, times of day, layouts. A variation is read from the JSON file sitting next to the map file, and a separate «Original» entry restores the starting look. What exactly gets replaced is controlled by the «Variations: swap scope» setting, from the background alone to the full environment. Tokens and anything added by hand survive every scope. GM only.

SwapScope.Name: Variations: swap scope
SwapScope.Hint: What to change when a variation has a sidecar JSON. Tokens and anything added manually are always preserved.
SwapScope.Base: Basic: background, walls, tiles, sounds, light
SwapScope.Full: Full environment (+ lighting, drawings, notes, templates, regions)

Notify.GMOnly: Only the GM can switch scenes.
Notify.InProgress: A swap is still running — please wait.
Notify.NoFile: This variation has no file set.
Notify.BadJson: Variation JSON could not be read: {label}
Notify.FilePickerError: Could not open the file picker.

ADM_LEVELS.settings.backgroundFreeze.hin: A snowflake button in the tiles tools: freezes/resumes the animated scene background video, showing the same frame to all players (frame synced). State stored per scene. GM only.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.filePreview.name: File preview in picker
ADM_LEVELS.settings.filePreview.hint: In the File Picker, on hover: plays sounds (loop), shows image thumbnails and webm video with timing. Plus recursive subfolder search (walks nested folders and shows matches from them).
ADM_LEVELS.settings.sceneExportName.name: Scene export name
ADM_LEVELS.settings.sceneExportName.hint: When exporting a scene to JSON, names the file after the background map (no folder/extension) instead of «fvtt-Scene-…-id». E.g. background Stonehenge_[ocean].webm → Stonehenge_[ocean].json. No background — default name.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.sceneQuickExport.hin: A scene context menu item after «Export Data»: after confirmation it saves the scene export straight into the folder holding the scene's background image or video, with no save dialog. A file with the same name is overwritten. The file content and name are the same as a normal export. GM only.
ADM_LEVELS.quickExport.title: Quick export
ADM_LEVELS.quickExport.confirm: Quick-export scene «{name}» into the scene files folder?
ADM_LEVELS.quickExport.failed: Could not export scene «{name}» — see the console for details.
ADM_LEVELS.quickExport.noFolder: The scene has no background in Foundry data — nowhere to save.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.sceneFolderImport.hi: A button in the Scenes list between «Create Scene» and «Create Folder»: pick a folder in Foundry data — every scene JSON export in it and its subfolders is imported, each as a separate scene, exactly like a manual «Import Data». GM only.
ADM_LEVELS.sceneImport.title: Import scenes from folder
ADM_LEVELS.sceneImport.onlyData: Pick a folder in Foundry data (Data).
ADM_LEVELS.sceneImport.rootRefused: Pick a specific folder: the data root holds every module and world.
ADM_LEVELS.sceneImport.truncated: The scan stopped at {n} folders — pick a narrower folder.
ADM_LEVELS.sceneImport.none: No scene exports found in «{folder}» (JSON files: {json}).
ADM_LEVELS.sceneImport.confirm: Found {n} scenes in «{folder}». Each will be created as a separate scene and imported. Continue?
ADM_LEVELS.sceneImport.doneFailed: Imported: {ok}, failed: {fail} ({names}). See the console for details.
ADM_LEVELS.sceneImport.error: Scene folder import was interrupted — see the console for details.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tileScroll.name: Tile scroll
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tileScroll.hint: In the tile config (spoiler «Tile scroll») — animated texture scrolling: direction in degrees, speed, and «Feather edge» (transparent gradient at the tile borders so scrolling has no hard cutoff). A lightweight own alternative to parallax-tiles / tile-scroll.
ADM_LEVELS.tileScroll.title: Tile scroll (ADMaps)
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tilePartialFade.name: Partial tile fade
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tilePartialFade.hint: Adds «Partial fade» to the tile occlusion list: on hover a roof dissolves in front of the doors and windows under it (so their place shows) and where the token looks through an open door or a window. Along blind walls and behind closed doors the roof stays. Tokens under the roof (with their name, effects and bars) show only where the roof is dissolved. On a tile without partial fade the same box is called «Black shadow under the tile»: the tile's see-through parts (sail shadows, rope edges) do not reveal what the token cannot see — the shadow under them matches the shadow around, and the tile itself stays on top (needs Better Roofs with «Reveals Fog of War»). Hovered, such a tile fades whole and shows the shadow under it.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tilePartialFadeOutli: While a roof is hover-faded, the edge of the cut gets a black line — so it is clear what is roof and what is inside. The line runs only where the roof goes on past the edge.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tilePartialFadeShado: Partial fade: inner shadow of the cut
While a roof is hover-faded, a soft shadow falls from the cut edge inward — as if the roof cast it into the room. Adds a sense of depth.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tileHoverLink.name: Better Roofs link on hover
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tileHoverLink.hint: Better Roofs fades linked tiles («Occlusion Link Id») only while a token stands under the source tile. With this tool they also fade while the cursor hovers the source — together with it and just as smoothly. For example, a mast over the forecastle hides while the forecastle roof is hover-dissolved: give the roof an Id and check «Occlusion Link Source?», give the mast the same Id without the check.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.tilePartialFadeHideO: Partial fade: hide tokens on the roof

Tokens standing on the roof inside the cut fade out with the roof while it is hovered — otherwise they seem to stand inside the room. Point at the token itself and the roof comes back together with it.
ADM_LEVELS.tileScroll.worldHint: The image is not stretched: it repeats at its own size and is anchored to the scene, so neighbouring tiles continue each other without a seam. Speed is in pixels per second. The pattern size is the usual Tile Scale (Appearance tab): 0.5 = twice as small; the tile itself stays whole.
ADM_LEVELS.tileScroll.patternRotationHin: Turns the pattern clockwise (Pattern mode only). Neighbouring tiles with the same angle still join without a seam. The scroll direction stays in scene degrees: to scroll along a turned road, give the direction the same angle.
ADM_LEVELS.tileScroll.edgeStyleHint: Straight: plain feathering. Torn: an uneven edge on all sides, like torn paper. Brush stroke: as if painted with a brush from right to left - top and bottom nearly straight, dry bristle streaks on the left. A shaped edge turns feathering on by itself; the feather width sets how far it reaches. Every tile gets its own shape.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.sceneRecord.name: Scene recording
ADM_LEVELS.settings.sceneRecord.hint: Right-click a scene in the navbar → «Record scene»: fits the zoom to the scene bounds and records the canvas (without Foundry's UI) for the set time into a data folder. Duration is set below. GM only, active scene.
ADM_LEVELS.sceneRecord.durationHint: How many seconds to record on «Record scene». The countdown starts once the camera has already been fitted to the scene bounds, so all of that time lands in the video. Recording stops on its own and the file goes into the data folder.
ADM_LEVELS.sceneRecord.audioHint: Record the «Environment» and «Interface» audio channels into the video. Music (the playlist channel) is intentionally not recorded. Levels are as heard, after the volume sliders.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.cinema.name: ADMaps Cinema
ADM_LEVELS.settings.cinema.hint: Cinematic camera for this client: zoom-in on token click, auto-zoom to fit targets with UI paddings, follow on movement. The camera never leaves the scene bounds. Per-player setting — each player enables it for themselves; options below.
ADM_LEVELS.cinema.clickZoomHint: Smooth camera zoom-in onto the token you just selected. How close is set by «Cinema: zoom level». The camera never leaves the scene bounds, so near the map edges the zoom-in comes out weaker.
ADM_LEVELS.cinema.clickScaleHint: Canvas scale for the zoom-in (1 = 100%). Also caps how close the target auto-zoom gets.
ADM_LEVELS.cinema.targetZoomHint: When the selected token targets someone, the camera fits it and all targets with the configured screen-edge paddings.
ADM_LEVELS.cinema.padHint: Frame padding for the target auto-zoom, in screen pixels. It exists for the UI that covers the map: chat on the right, tool palette on the left, navbar on top. Anything inside the padding is not counted as visible, so the camera pulls back further.
ADM_LEVELS.cinema.followHint: While a token is selected, the camera smoothly follows its movement (and targets). While the target stands still, manual map panning is respected.
ADM_LEVELS.filePreview.shown: Shown {n}{more}. Refine the query for completeness.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.massEditMirrorFix.hi: Completes Mass Edit's built-in mirroring (Shift+D → H/V, and the same keys while placing a preset): recomputes the direction of our regions — plateaus and stairs. Without it a mirrored building ends up with its ascent pointing the wrong way. Mass Edit's method is patched in memory; its files are left untouched. Requires a reload when toggled.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.teleportPair.name: Paired region teleport
ADM_LEVELS.settings.teleportPair.hint: Button on the Regions layer: opens a window where two dropdowns pick regions of the same scene — the teleport is created both ways with "Ask for confirmation" enabled. No canvas selection needed (you cannot select two regions there anyway). Regions sharing a name are numbered so they can be told apart. Running it again creates no duplicate: if one direction already exists, only the missing one is added.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.teleportStepBack.hin: The built-in «Teleport Token» stops a token exactly where its center crosses the region edge — off the grid. Answer «No» in the «Teleport?» dialog (or close it) and the token stays on that edge; when the edge runs along a wall, it stays in the wall and cannot walk out. With this tool the token then returns to the last cell of its path before the region — instantly and through walls. An accepted teleport is left as is.
ADM_LEVELS.teleportPair.sameRegion: The same region is selected twice.
ADM_LEVELS.teleportPair.already: These regions are already linked by a teleport.
ADM_LEVELS.teleportPair.completed: Added the reverse direction — the link is now two-way.
ADM_LEVELS.teleportPair.failed: Could not create the teleport — see the console.
ADM_LEVELS.teleportPair.note: The teleport is created both ways, with "Ask for confirmation" enabled.
ADM_LEVELS.teleportPair.needTwoOnScene: The scene needs at least two regions.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.activeAdventure.name: Active adventure
ADM_LEVELS.settings.activeAdventure.hint: Right-click a folder in the Scenes list -> "Active adventure": marks the destination folder. Then right-click a scene in the navigation bar -> "Copy and view": copies the scene into the marked folder, asks for a name and switches you to the copy (without activating it, so players stay put). Keeps template scenes clean. GM only.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.levelsFollowToken.hi: While a token is selected, the Levels floor panel follows its elevation: climb to the roof and the panel switches to the roof floor by itself. Deselecting keeps you on that floor. Players do not need this — their perspective already follows their token. Requires the Levels module. Client setting.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.levelsPanelAltW.name: Floor panel on Alt+W
ADM_LEVELS.settings.levelsPanelAltW.hint: The Levels floor panel stays hidden and appears together with walls and regions on Alt+W — one switch for all map scaffolding. It does not open on scenes with no floors configured. Client setting.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.levelsGhostTokens.hi: With no token selected, Levels hides everyone who is not on the current floor, so the GM loses the overview. With this enabled they fade to semi-transparent instead of vanishing: the whole map stays visible and off-floor tokens are obvious at a glance. Nothing changes while a token is selected — Levels already shows everything then. GM only, client setting.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.ghostTokensAlpha.hin: How visible tokens on other floors are. Lower is fainter, 100 looks like a normal token. The value applies immediately, no reload needed. It only matters while «Other floors: ghosts» is enabled, and only where that option works at all: for the GM, with no token selected. A token separated from you by a floor is still not shown — ghosts do not shine through decking.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.levelsEffectFloors.h: Sequencer knows nothing about floors, so animations show up for everyone: a wall of fire on the ground floor is visible to people on the roof. With this enabled an effect is hidden while its floor is not yours and comes back when you move to that floor — persistent zones are never lost, they simply appear once you get there. An effect's floor comes from the elevation it was placed at. Requires the Levels module: without it there are no floors to sort by. Client setting.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.levelsFloorTransit.h: Dragging a token from a roof down to the ground writes the final elevation immediately and only then animates the position, so from the very first frame the token dips under the roof tile and travels across the lower floor in plain sight — ugly, and a spoiler for rooms nobody has entered yet. With this enabled the rendered elevation stays where it was for the duration of the move: the token walks along the roof as if it were not leaving it and descends at the end of the path. The VISION elevation is held to the end of the path as well, otherwise the player would see the lower floor halfway through. Only the visuals change — distance, regions and movement history are computed as usual. Moving straight down in place is not affected. Requires the Levels module. Client setting.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.levelsStairGate.name: Disable Levels stairs
ADM_LEVELS.settings.levelsStairGate.hint: A Levels stair region (Execute Script → RegionHandler.stair) looks at elevation only: match the edge of its range and the token is instantly moved to the other end. It checks neither the movement action nor the player's intent, and in our scenes elevation is owned by ADMaps Tools regions — together they produce jumps nobody can explain (a climbing token at 15 ft crossing a 0-15 stair drops to the bottom). With this enabled those scripts do not fire. The regions and their behaviors stay untouched in the scene: turn the setting off and the old behavior returns.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.levelsFastRoofFade.h: Walking into a building takes almost a second for the roof to disappear. That is not the roof module nor Levels — it is core: a 250 ms delay plus a 750 ms fade animation. With this enabled the fade starts immediately and is nearly instant. Custom values via __ADM_ROOF_FADE = { delay: 0, duration: 0 } in the console. Turn it off and the factory values return. Client setting.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.doorUnderToken.name: Door under a token
ADM_LEVELS.settings.doorUnderToken.hint: The door icon sits on top of the map and catches the click first: if a token stands in the doorway you cannot grab it with the mouse — every click opens or closes the door. With this enabled the icon under a visible token stops catching clicks and they reach the token instead. The door stays visible and works as usual once the token steps aside. A token a floor above or below the door does not block it.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.regionFromTile.name: Region from tile
ADM_LEVELS.settings.regionFromTile.hint: A button in the region tools: press it, then click a tile on the scene — a plateau region is traced from the tile opacity. The elevation range equals the tile elevation (15 becomes 15-15) and the plateau height matches. A cell is taken whole when more than half of it is opaque; a bevelled edge yields a half-cell triangle; shadows, sparks and stray grass are dropped. It does not bind the region to the tile — that is easier to finish by hand.
ADM_LEVELS.regionFromTile.pick: Click a tile on the scene (Esc to cancel).
ADM_LEVELS.settings.doorMeshElevation.hi: A door with a texture is drawn as a separate sprite, and walls have no elevation field — the core pushes the leaf almost up to the foreground, so a ground-floor door shows THROUGH the roof. This option gives the leaf the elevation of its floor's TOP (ceiling from Wall Height, otherwise the floor top from the Levels panel) so roofs cover it again. Applies automatically and live: nothing is written to the scene, and a manually set core.elevation flag is left alone.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.doorSwingPreview.hin: A thin arc with an arrow and a hinge dot over a door: which way and from which side it opens. Shown for the door being edited while its wall config is open, and for every door on the scene with Alt+W.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.doorInvert.name: Invert door
ADM_LEVELS.settings.doorInvert.hint: An «Invert» button after «Open Direction» in the door settings: swaps the door's end points so it opens from the other end. A swinging door still opens to the same side; a sliding one retracts towards the other end.
ADM_LEVELS.doorInvert.label: Hinge
ADM_LEVELS.doorInvert.hint: Swaps the door's end points: it will open from the other end. Unsaved edits in this window are saved along with it.
ADM_LEVELS.doorInvert.double: A double door has hinges at both ends — nothing to swap.
ADM_LEVELS.doorInvert.midpoint: This animation pivots around the middle of the door — nothing to swap.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.doorQuick.name: Quick door
ADM_LEVELS.settings.doorQuick.hint: A «Quick door» button after «Door Type» in the wall config: the wall becomes an ordinary wooden door at once — with a sound, a swing animation and a texture, as on ADMaps maps.
ADM_LEVELS.doorQuick.hint: Makes the wall a wooden door at once: sound, swing, texture. Unsaved edits in this window are saved along with it.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.moveWallElevation.na: Walls during movement use waypoint elevation
ADM_LEVELS.settings.moveWallElevation.hi: While moving, height-limited walls (wall-height) are tested at the elevation of the path waypoint — a stair step, a plateau — rather than where the token stood when the move began. Without it a token that climbed the stairs stopped at the plateau wall.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.regionElevation.name: Elevation regions
ADM_LEVELS.settings.regionElevation.hint: Plateaus, stairs, water and transport: region-based elevation snapping, the type selector in the region window and ramp arrows. Turn off if you only need the module's other features. Elevation of existing tokens is NOT changed — they simply stop snapping; region flags are kept, so turning it back on restores everything. World setting, requires reload.
ADM_LEVELS.activeAdventure.folderGone: The active adventure folder is gone — no copy was made.
ADM_LEVELS.activeAdventure.cloneFailed: Could not copy the scene — see the console (F12) for details.
ADM_LEVELS.activeAdventure.cloneEmpty: Copy not created — the original is untouched. See the console (F12) for details.
ADM_LEVELS.activeAdventure.createdNoView: "{name}" was created in "{folder}", but switching to it failed — open it manually.
ADM_LEVELS.tools.supersededIntro: These modules are now built into ADMaps Tools and have been disabled to avoid duplicates:
ADM_LEVELS.tools.supersededReloadNow: Reload the application now to apply?
ADM_LEVELS.tools.supersededReloadLater: The changes will apply after the next reload.
ADM_LEVELS.regionFromTile.needGrid: Region from tile: the scene needs a grid.
ADM_LEVELS.regionFromTile.noImage: Region from tile: could not read the tile image.
ADM_LEVELS.regionFromTile.noOpaque: Region from tile: no opaque cells found. Debug: __ADM_REGION_DEBUG = true
ADM_LEVELS.regionFromTile.failed: Region from tile: failed, see the console for details.
ADM_LEVELS.sceneRecord.maybeNotSaved: The recording may not have been saved ({path}) — see the console.
ADM_LEVELS.sceneRecord.saveFailed: Could not save the scene recording (see the console).
ADM_LEVELS.sceneRecord.alreadyRunning: Scene recording is already in progress.
ADM_LEVELS.sceneRecord.gmOnly: Scene recording is available to the GM only.
ADM_LEVELS.sceneRecord.captureUnsupporte: Canvas capture is not supported by this client.
ADM_LEVELS.sceneRecord.dsnCaptureEnabled: Dice So Nice: dice capture mode enabled — the dice will appear in recordings after a reload (F5).
ADM_LEVELS.sceneRecord.emptyRecording: The recording is empty (0 bytes) — see the console.
ADM_LEVELS.sceneRecord.encoderLagged: Scene recording: the encoder couldn't keep up — the file holds {got} s out of {total} s. Reduce the window size or the duration.
ADM_LEVELS.sceneRecord.mediaRecorderUnsu: The browser/client does not support video recording (MediaRecorder).
ADM_LEVELS.settings.wallChainClick.name: Wall chain by clicks
ADM_LEVELS.settings.wallChainClick.hint: A toggle in the wall tools. While it is on: a click continues the wall from the previous point (a click near an existing wall endpoint lands exactly on it); Shift + click places a point exactly under the cursor, off the grid. A drag with the button held traces the cursor through grid intersections only — straight runs (including diagonals) become one wall, a turn starts a new one, going back over a wall draws nothing; a drag pressed next to the chain end continues the chain. Right click or Esc closes the chain without touching what is already drawn, and a «+ Region» button appears at its first point: press it, then click a region to add the outline to it or an empty spot to create a new region (its window opens); Ctrl+Z right after reverts that. Existing walls are not interactive (their endpoints cannot be grabbed) — the Select tool works as usual. Turn the toggle off for the stock behaviour. Client setting.
ADM_LEVELS.wallChain.regionButtonHint: Make a region from this outline: then click a region to add to it, or an empty spot for a new one
ADM_LEVELS.wallChain.regionPick: Click a region or an empty spot
ADM_LEVELS.wallChain.regionCancelHint: Esc or right click to cancel
ADM_LEVELS.wallChain.regionMerged: The outline was added to the region "{name}".
ADM_LEVELS.wallChain.regionUndoMerge: The outline was taken back from the region "{name}".
ADM_LEVELS.wallChain.regionFailed: Could not build the region, see the console.
ADM_LEVELS.settings.updateNotice.name: Update notice
ADM_LEVELS.settings.updateNotice.hint: When a newer ADMaps Tools release is out, the GM gets a window on load: the installed and the new version and how to update. «Don't show again» hides it until the next release.
ADM_LEVELS.updateNotice.title: ADMaps Tools: update available
ADM_LEVELS.updateNotice.body: A new version of ADMaps Tools is out: {latest}. You have {current}.
ADM_LEVELS.updateNotice.how: To update, return to Setup, open Add-on Modules and update ADMaps Tools.
